item.title: How to use n8n for free: build your first AI agent, step by step
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The self-hosted Community edition is free. With Node.js 20.19 to 24 installed, run npx n8n. Then open localhost:5678 in your browser. Docker works too. Go to aistudio.google.com/app/apikey and click Create API key in new project. In n8n, open the Gemini model node, pick Create New Credential, paste the key, save. Sources: n8n Docs: Choose your n8n, n8n Docs: Install with npm, n8n Docs: Install with Docker, n8n: Build your first AI agent (template), n8n Blog: How to build your first AI agent, Techsy: n8n AI agents tutorial.

If you are comfortable typing a command in a terminal, the free edition is enough for this guide. If you register your email in the free edition, n8n unlocks a few extras: folders, debug in editor and custom execution data.","sources":[{"name":"n8n Docs: Choose your n8n","url":"https://docs.n8n.io/choose-n8n/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"One more cost to know about: the AI model is billed separately from n8n. A tutorial from Techsy notes that the self-hosted Community edition has no execution limits, but any OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini usage is charged by that provider. The Gemini key in this guide is free to create, which makes it the cheapest way to start.","sources":[{"name":"Techsy: n8n AI agents tutorial","url":"https://techsy.io/blog/n8n-ai-agents-tutorial"},{"name":"n8n: Build your first AI agent (template)","url":"https://n8n.io/workflows/6270-build-your-first-ai-agent/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Step by step: your first n8n AI agent","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Install and start n8n","text":"Install Node.js, version 20.19 to 24.x according to n8n's docs. Then open a terminal and run npx n8n to try it without installing anything, or npm install n8n -g followed by n8n start to keep it. Open http://localhost:5678 in your browser. n8n's docs say npm installs are deprecated starting with n8n 3.0, so if you plan to keep using it, the Docker route is the safer long-term setup.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Or start it with Docker","text":"With Docker Desktop installed, create a volume with docker volume create n8n_data, then run the n8nio/n8n image with port 5678 open and that volume mounted to /home/node/.n8n, as the install page shows. Set GENERIC_TIMEZONE to your time zone so scheduled workflows run at the right hour. n8n's docs now point to Docker Compose as the recommended method for a lasting setup.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Get a free Google AI API key","text":"Go to aistudio.google.com/app/apikey, click Create API key in new project and copy the key. n8n's starter template says this free key is the only thing you need to bring.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Load the starter agent and add the key","text":"Open the Build your first AI agent template from n8n's template library. On the canvas, open the node named Connect your model (Google Gemini), choose Create New Credential in the Credential dropdown, paste the key into the API Key field and click Save. The template already wires a Chat Trigger to an AI Agent node, plus a Simple Memory node for follow-up questions and two tools: Get Weather and Get News, which reads an RSS feed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Open the chat and test it","text":"Go to the Example Chat node and click Open Chat in its panel. Ask for the weather in Paris, then ask for the latest tech news. A weather answer shows the Get Weather tool works; a list of headlines shows Get News works. Ask a follow-up question about the same city to check that memory is doing its job.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Build it yourself instead of using the template","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"n8n's blog walks through the same pieces by hand. Click the plus button on an empty canvas and add a Chat Trigger. Add an AI Agent node and connect the trigger to it. In the agent, choose Connected Chat Trigger Node as the source of the user message. Add a chat model node, such as Google Gemini, OpenAI or Anthropic, create its credential and connect it to the agent's Chat Model input. Tools go into the agent's Tool input.","sources":[{"name":"n8n Blog: How to build your first AI agent","url":"https://blog.n8n.io/how-to-build-ai-agent/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The agent's behavior lives in the System Message, under Options in the AI Agent node. n8n's guide suggests stating the task, explaining when and how to use each tool, and adding constraints. Rename each tool node so its name matches the name you use in the System Message.","sources":[{"name":"n8n Blog: How to build your first AI agent","url":"https://blog.n8n.io/how-to-build-ai-agent/"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A starter System Message","text":"You are a research assistant.
When the user asks about the weather, call the [weather tool name] tool.
When the user asks for news, call the [news tool name] tool and return the 3 most relevant headlines with one line each.
If no tool fits the question, say you cannot check that. Never guess.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"After every test, open the execution in n8n and look at the AI Agent node's input and output. n8n's guide recommends this to see which tools the agent actually called. If it skipped a tool, the fix is usually a clearer System Message or a better description on the tool.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where n8n agents struggle","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Techsy tutorial reports that agents get confused once they have more than about five to seven tools, that they can fail without an obvious error, and that n8n gives less control over agent design than code frameworks such as LangGraph or CrewAI.","sources":[{"name":"Techsy: n8n AI agents tutorial","url":"https://techsy.io/blog/n8n-ai-agents-tutorial"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"n8n is a workflow tool first, and it shows. The practical answer is the same as with any agent: one narrow job, a few tools, and a test run before you trust it with anything real.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Keep your first agent read-only. Weather, news and summaries cannot do damage. Add tools that send email or write to a database only after you have watched a few executions and the agent calls the right tool every time.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Anthropic just launched its own Excel rival, and Microsoft stock dropped the same day
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 10, Anthropic launched Claude Sheets in beta: a spreadsheet built right into Claude. Claude adds tabs, formulas, formatting and charts, and edits cells next to you. It shows every change it makes. Paid plans, beta. Exports to Excel. Claude Meetings puts Claude in video calls as a visible participant. It drafts the plan, answers in the chat and pulls numbers from work apps. It starts on Google Meet for Team and Enterprise plans. Sources: TechCrunch, Engadget, Yahoo Finance, Investing.com via Yahoo Finance, Claude Help Center.

item.title: How to use CapCut AI: captions, scripts and clips in minutes
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On desktop: import your video, open the Text tab, click Auto captions, pick the language and click Create. The captions land on the timeline, ready to edit. Read every line. Accents, noise and names trip the AI up. On the web, the Styles tab has looks like Glow, or let Style captions with AI pick one. Sources: CapCut: How to add subtitles in CapCut, CapCut: AI Clip Maker, CapCut: Script to video maker, CapCut Help Center: Standard vs Pro, CapCut Help Center: new subscription pricing, Descript.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use CapCut AI: auto captions, AI video maker and clipper","dek":"Step by step instructions for the three CapCut AI tools people use most, and what each one needs from your plan.","summary":"CapCut's AI tools can add captions to a video, turn a script into a first draft and cut a long video into short clips. On desktop: import your video","text":"Open CapCut on your computer and start a new project. Create the captions","text":"Open the Text tab at the top and click Auto captions. In the pop up, choose the language spoken in the video and click Create. On the web: use AI captions","text":"On the CapCut web start page, find the You may want to try section and click AI captions. Upload a video from your computer or your CapCut cloud space. Then click Export, or Edit more to open the full editor.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. CapCut builds a first draft from stock footage. Open it in the multi track editor to swap clips for your own, adjust captions, transitions and the voiceover, and set the shape of the video. Then click Export, name the project, choose resolution, frame rate and format, and download it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Be realistic about this one. A draft made of stock footage looks like a draft made of stock footage. It is a fast way to get timing and structure, and a poor way to get something that feels like yours. Replace at least the opening shots with your own material.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to cut a long video into shorts with the AI Clip Maker","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Upload the long video","text":"Upload from your computer, CapCut cloud, Google Drive or Dropbox, and keep the page open until the upload finishes. CapCut suggests the tool for video podcasts, lessons, commentary and speeches, where people talk on camera.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Let it find the highlights","text":"The AI Clip Maker picks the strongest moments and cuts them into short clips. CapCut says it can also crop a wide 16:9 video to vertical 9:16 while tracking the speaker, and add captions. Before you export, you can change clip length and apply templates.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Check, edit, export","text":"Click Preview to watch each clip. Click Edit more to trim or fix one in the editor. Click Export to save it or share it straight to social media.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"The AI picks moments from speech, so a clip can start mid thought or end before the punchline. Watch the first and last three seconds of every clip and trim by hand. Those six seconds decide whether anyone keeps watching.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What CapCut AI is good at, and what it is not","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"CapCut AI is good at the boring parts of short video: getting words on screen, finding the clip worth posting and turning a wide video into a vertical one. Use it to get to a first version fast, then spend your own time on the opening seconds and the captions, because that is where viewers decide.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Google just released its strongest AI yet. It found hidden security holes in under 2 hours
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 10, Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon to the public. It calls it its strongest model for cybersecurity and long, multi-step work. It sits above Gemini 4 Argon and is meant for the hardest jobs, like complex debugging. Google says security firm Wiz used Carbon to scan two major software providers. It found unknown 0-day flaws in under two hours, work Google says normally takes weeks. For two weeks before launch, only selected security defenders had it. Sources: Google, 9to5Google, Digital Trends, Runtime Wire.

Axiom Bio used the model to identify toxicity mechanisms its team had not found before and is moving production scientific analyses to Carbon and Argon, according to the same report.","sources":[{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-gemini-4-carbon-is-now-available-for-complex-ai-tasks/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Developers also get an early look at a feature called /swarm in Google Antigravity, in which Carbon handles design, coordination and review while lighter, faster models work on other tasks in parallel, Digital Trends reported.","sources":[{"name":"Digital Trends","url":"https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-gemini-4-carbon-is-now-available-for-complex-ai-tasks/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Who can use it and what it costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google AI Ultra subscribers can use Carbon in the Gemini app, in AI Mode in Search and in Google Antigravity, with the app rollout starting on November 10, according to 9to5Google. Developers can reach it through the paid tier of the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Android Studio, and businesses through Gemini for business. Scientists can apply for six months of free access to Argon and Carbon, and cybersecurity defenders can apply to the Fairwind Program.","sources":[{"name":"Google","url":"https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemini-4-carbon-developers/"},{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/10/gemini-app-4-carbon/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Introductory API pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, according to 9to5Google and Runtime Wire. 9to5Google reported that the price then rises to $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens.","sources":[{"name":"9to5Google","url":"https://9to5google.com/2026/11/10/gemini-app-4-carbon/"},{"name":"Runtime Wire","url":"https://runtimewire.com/article/google-gemini-4-carbon-now-available"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The launch puts the security claims at the center of the pitch. The benchmark rankings and the Wiz and Axiom Bio results come from Google and its partners, not from independent testing, so outside evaluations over the coming weeks will show how much of the advantage holds up. The short introductory window also gives developers a cheap period to compare Carbon with Argon and with rival models before the price doubles.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The next signal to watch is independent benchmark results and developer reports on whether Carbon's higher token use still delivers a lower cost per task once the price rises on December 1.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use DeepSeek safely: the settings to change and what never to type
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: DeepSeek's privacy policy says it stores what it collects on servers in China. That includes your prompts, uploaded files and chat history. Type nothing you would not want stored there. On the web, open Settings, then Data, and switch off the option to improve the model for everyone. In the app, Kaspersky found the same switch under Settings, then Data controls. Sources: DeepSeek Privacy Policy, DeepSeek API Docs: DeepSeek V4 Preview Release, Kaspersky, DeleteMe, The Hacker News, Wikipedia: DeepSeek (chatbot).

item.title: How to build your first Zapier AI agent for free, step by step
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Sign in at agents.zapier.com. Take the tour, or use the + icon in the sidebar and pick New agent. Describe the job in plain English or start from a template. Choose what starts the agent: on demand, on a schedule, from a Zap or from another app. Example: a new lead arrives, the agent sums it up and emails sales. Open Insert tools, then Add tool. Add data sources like Google Drive or Notion, and actions like a Gmail draft. Sources: Zapier: Zapier Agents guide, Zapier Help Center: How is Zapier Agents usage measured?, Zapier Agents pricing, Zapier: Zapier Agents overview, XRAY Tech.

item.title: Anthropic just set its real IPO price: about $1 trillion
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 10, Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow at $70 to $78 a share. It is selling 825 million shares, most of them new. Reuters says that raises up to $64.4 billion. Late on November 9, bankers got IPO details that Anthropic quickly took back, Reuters reported. That version said up to $80 a share. The new top price is $78. That is Reuters' math from the filing. Anthropic's last private value was $965 billion. Sources: Reuters, Anthropic, RTTNews, Reuters via Investing.com, Malay Mail (AFP).

item.title: Anthropic sent bankers its IPO price. Then took it back
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 9, Anthropic sent bankers a filing pricing its IPO at $70 to $80 a share, Reuters reported. A second email said the pricing was "inaccurate" and a new filing would follow. It did not say what was wrong. The filing listed about 867 million shares. At $80 each, that raises $69.3 billion. One analyst put the implied value near $1.4 trillion. Investors once talked about $2 trillion. The filing also showed $26 billion from Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC. Sources: Reuters, Stocktwits, Business Standard.

item.title: OpenAI built a 35-second kill switch for its own AI after one took 2.5 hours to stop
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI unveiled Control Room on November 9: one central system that tracks every AI job running across its research labs. When safety or security worries come up, it can stop them fast. Each job gets an ID. Before a model answers, the system checks that the job is still allowed. Once someone or a monitor orders a stop, the model refuses to answer that job. OpenAI says the longest gap between a stop order and the AI going quiet is 35 seconds, because of a cache. Sources: Interesting Engineering, RuntimeWire, The Next Web.

item.title: Google's own help page says human reviewers may see parts of your Gmail and Drive through Gemini
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Google's Gemini help page says a subset of data from connected apps like Gmail and Drive is reviewed by human reviewers. item.author: NeuraFeed news desk

item.title: Meta says its new AI model matches Claude Haiku for a third of the cost
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Meta Superintelligence Lab released Muse Ember on November 9. Meta calls it the lab's lightest and most cost-efficient model yet. It is built for repetitive agent work: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, data extraction and long documents. On the independent Artificial Analysis index, Ember scores 36, level with Claude Haiku 5.5. OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna scores 28. Meta puts Ember's cost per index task at about $0.14, versus $0.41 for Haiku. Ember is not best everywhere. On FrontierCode 2.0, a coding test, Haiku scores 34.9% and Ember 27.2%. Sources: TechCrunch, The Next Web.

item.title: Apple just started charging extra for its AI
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Apple is now selling its first paid add-on for Apple Intelligence: a $49.99 intelligence usage pack inside Logic Pro 13. It is a one-time purchase, not a subscription, and only kicks in after you hit your monthly AI limit. The packs are for Apple Creator Studio subscribers, who already pay $12.99 a month or $129 a year. Apple's support page does not say how much AI use the $49.99 actually buys. Packs do not work with Family Sharing. Unused usage rolls over each month but expires 12 months after purchase. Sources: 9to5Mac, Tech Between the Lines.

item.description: Skyfall AI calls Steve "the world's first AI CEO." It runs online businesses like SaaS products and Shopify apps with a team of AI agents. Every move comes with a forecast. item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Malbear Labs found the attacker's workspace exposed online during a routine sweep, with 70+ session transcripts and the agent's own reports. It ran on DeepSeek Flash with a 78,000 character jailbreak. When security software blocked an exploit, the agent switched methods without being told. When a tunneling tool was blocked, it wrote a replacement. The operator's messages were short: "Go on." "Stop." The agent's reports claim it reached millions of patient records through a database still using default passwords. Sources: Infosecurity Magazine, Malbear Labs.

item.title: Trump says the DOJ warned a top AI boss: get ready to go to jail

item.description: On CBS's 60 Minutes on November 8, Trump said AI risk can be managed, and named the Justice Department as the one doing it. item.title: Midjourney prompts that actually work: 5 rules from its own docs
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: undefined... Sources: Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics, Midjourney Docs: Parameter List, Midjourney Docs: Models, Midjourney Docs: Getting Started Guide, Visually AI (Heather Cooper): Midjourney V8 is live on alpha, Evolink: Midjourney V8.1 prompt guide.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Midjourney prompts: how to write image prompts that work","dek":"Midjourney rewards short, precise prompts and a few settings placed at the end. Here is what its own documentation recommends, with prompts to copy.","summary":"Midjourney's documentation says short, simple prompts usually produce the best images, with exact numbers, precise words and only the details you care about. Settings such as aspect ratio go at the end of the prompt, and the --no parameter removes things you do not want.","seo_title":"Midjourney prompts: how to write image prompts that work","seo_description":"Write better Midjourney prompts: keep them short, use exact numbers, pick the details that matter, put parameters at the end and remove things with --no.","answer_summary":"Write a short description of the image you want with precise words and exact numbers, add only the details that matter (subject, medium, setting, lighting, color, mood, composition), then put parameters like --ar 16:9 at the end.","tags":["Midjourney","AI images","Prompts","Image generation","AI guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney turns a written description into images. You type a prompt into the Imagine bar on the Create page at midjourney.com, press Enter, and it makes a set of four images. You need a paid plan before you can make your first image, according to Midjourney's Getting Started Guide.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Getting Started Guide","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/hc/en-us/articles/33329261836941-Getting-Started-Guide"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short version of this guide: write less than you think, choose exact words, say how many of something you want, describe what should be in the picture rather than what should not, and put settings at the very end. Everything below comes from Midjourney's own documentation, plus notes from people who test new versions.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Start with a short prompt","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney's Prompt Basics page is blunt about length. Short, simple prompts usually produce the best images. It suggests thinking of a prompt as a quick snapshot of the idea, and it warns that long lists and detailed instructions can confuse the process. A prompt can be as small as one word. With fewer details you get more variety; with more details you get more control.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The docs give an example. A long, chatty request for blooming California poppies in bright orange, drawn with colored pencils, becomes one plain line.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The short version","text":"Colored pencil illustration of bright orange California poppies","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Choose exact words and numbers","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Word choice matters. The docs recommend specific synonyms over generic ones, such as huge or enormous instead of big. Numbers matter even more. A plural like cats leaves the count up to Midjourney. Three cats, or a collective noun like a flock of birds, makes the result predictable.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Say how many","text":"Three cats asleep on a sunny windowsill, soft morning light","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Add only the details you care about","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"When certain parts of the image matter to you, name them. Midjourney's docs list seven areas to think about: subject (a person, animal, object or place), medium (photo, painting, illustration, sculpture, doodle), environment (indoors, underwater, in the city), lighting (soft, overcast, studio, neon), color (vibrant, muted, pastel, black and white), mood (calm, playful, gloomy, energetic) and composition (portrait, headshot, closeup, bird's-eye view).","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"You do not need all seven. Pick the two or three that decide whether the image works for you, and let Midjourney's default style handle the rest.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A detailed photo","text":"Closeup photo of [subject] [doing something] in [place], [lighting] light, [color] colors, [mood] mood","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Put parameters at the end","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Parameters are settings you type after the description. Midjourney's parameter list says they go at the end of the prompt, with a space before the two dashes and no commas or periods inside them. The most useful ones for beginners are --ar to change the shape of the image, --s (stylize) to control how much of Midjourney's own artistic style is applied, --chaos to get more varied results, and --raw for more control over the output.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For the current V8.1 model, a third-party prompt guide from Evolink lists the defaults: square 1:1 images, stylize at 100 on a scale of 0 to 1000, and chaos at 0 on a scale of 0 to 100. Stylize sets how strongly Midjourney's default look is applied, so lower values give a plainer result.","sources":[{"name":"Evolink: Midjourney V8.1 prompt guide","url":"https://evolink.ai/docs/en/api-manual/image-series/midjourney/midjourney-v8-1-prompt-guide"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A wide image with a bit more style","text":"Watercolor painting of a lighthouse on a cliff at sunset --ar 16:9 --s 250","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use --ar 4:5 or --ar 9:16 for images meant for a phone screen, and --ar 16:9 for slides and desktop wallpapers.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Say what you want, not what you do not want","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"This is the mistake most people make. If you write a party with no cake, the docs warn, you may still get a cake, because mentioning a thing can pull it into the image. Describe the scene you want instead. When you really need to remove something, use the --no parameter, which Midjourney's parameter list describes as the way to exclude elements from an image.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Prompt Basics","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/prompts"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Remove an object","text":"Minimal living room with a gray sofa and tall windows --no plants","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Pick the right model","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Midjourney's Models page lists V6, V6.1, V7 and V8.1, plus Niji 7 for anime and illustration. You can choose one for a single image by adding --v and the number at the end, for example --v 8.1, or set a default in the settings panel. V8.1 renders standard jobs several times faster than earlier versions, holds on to small details and can make 2K images with --hd. It does not support some older features, including Character Reference and Omni Reference.","sources":[{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Models","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/models"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Parameter List","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/parameter-list"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Testers report that newer models want clearer direction. Heather Cooper, who writes the Visually AI newsletter, found that V8 rewards more detail than V7 did, and she recommends switching to --raw for controlled or photorealistic results. Midjourney's docs say the same about Raw: it removes default styling for stronger prompt adherence.","sources":[{"name":"Visually AI (Heather Cooper): Midjourney V8 is live on alpha","url":"https://heatherbcooper.substack.com/p/midjourney-v8-is-live-on-alpha-heres"},{"name":"Midjourney Docs: Models","url":"https://docs.midjourney.com/docs/models"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Write the core line","text":"Describe the subject and the medium in one short sentence, such as a photo of a red bicycle against a white wall.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add two or three details","text":"Choose the lighting, mood or composition that matters most to you. Stop there.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Add parameters","text":"Set the shape with --ar, and add --raw if the result looks too stylized.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Change one thing at a time","text":"If the image is not right, change a single word or setting and run it again, so you know what made the difference.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Text inside the image","text":"Vintage travel poster for a mountain town with the words \"Visit Alpine Falls\" --v 8.1","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"For words inside an image, put the exact text in quotation marks. Cooper reports that V8 renders quoted text with higher accuracy.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Midjourney is good at mood, lighting and style, and a short prompt often gives a more striking result than a long one. It is weaker when you need exact control over many objects at once, and results still vary from run to run. Treat the first set of four images as a draft, keep the version you like, and refine from there.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Apple's new CEO reportedly pulled Craig Federighi into a closed-door meeting: move faster on AI
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In recent weeks, Apple CEO John Ternus met privately with software chief Craig Federighi, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported. His message: speed up the road map and go beyond just fixing Siri. Gurman says Ternus is frustrated by a reluctance to embrace AI with the same urgency as competitors. In public, Ternus praised the new Siri. In private, Gurman reports, he admits Apple is far behind. ChatGPT and Claude can already take over a computer to do tasks for you. Apple has nothing like it, Gurman notes. Sources: 9to5Mac, FourWeekMBA.

item.title: Anthropic quietly bought $3.4 billion of gas generators
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic agreed to pay $3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts of gas-fired generators, the Financial Times reported on November 8. Texas supplier OnePWR ordered the Caterpillar machines about two years earlier but needed money to finish the deal. The engines were ordered before prices surged. New orders now face lead times that stretch years ahead, the FT reported. Anthropic took over the orders and the install work. Where the machines will run is not known. Sources: The Next Web (Financial Times report), The Energy Mag, FourWeekMBA.
